tweets.text:
Ep 209 of Facts vs Feelings is here!

The bull market turned four this week 🎂

@sonusvarghese and I dig into what's driving it and where the stress is building

📈 The S&P 500 is up about 118% since October 2022, or 131% with dividends. Every bull market in the last 50 years that reached its third birthday went on to see a fifth.

💰 Profit growth accounts for roughly 85 points of the gain, about 40 of them from margin expansion. This year the forward P/E fell from about 22x to 19.5x as Treasury yields climbed, and earnings growth more than offset it.

💳 CCC spreads are near 900 bps. High yield overall is flat, and rate-hedged high yield and loans are beating cash. Ryan and Sonu see a duration problem from rising yields.

🏦 Hyperscaler bonds went from 1-2% of net new Treasury borrowing to about 14% in a year. SpaceX raised roughly $150B in four months, and its five-year CDS hit a record 200 bps.

🤖 Billions in AI compute contracts start billing between 2027 and 2029. Sonu flags 2027 and 2028 as the potential reckoning for the AI capex cycle.

We also cover small caps vs higher yields, the dollar back above 100 on the DXY, and next week's midterm episode with PIMCO's Libby Cantrell.

👇👇
https://t.co/0CiTg2e9Ns

BREAKING: Trading volume in the S&P 500 ETF, $SPY, fell to just 22.6 million shares on Friday, the lowest for a full trading day since November 25th, 2005.

Excluding sessions around market holidays, Friday's volume was the lowest since October 11th, 2004.

By comparison, volume fell below 20 million shares on December 24th, 2019, but that was during a half-day trading session.

On Monday, trading volume fell to just ~18 million shares, the lowest non-holiday reading since 2003.

As a result, the 5-day average of $SPY trading activity declined below 30 million shares, its lowest on record.

Meanwhile, the three previous low-volume periods in December 2024, February 2025, and August 2026 were each followed by an S&P 500 pullback.

Markets are in consolidation mode.

Northwood Space CEO Bridgit Mendler on building the infrastructure for 1,000 SpaceXs:

"I wanna see 1,000 SpaceXs. And I wanna see them not take 25 years to get there. I wanna see them get there in five years."

"I really believe that the best outcome for humanity is being able to have a real, open, unfettered, democratized space future."

"Being able to build infrastructure that introduces capabilities that so many different, not just companies, but countries can stand on, is really exciting."

"Think of cloud infrastructure and what it enabled for all of the internet-based companies. So many companies would not have been able to achieve that global reach if they had to think about deploying their own fiber and standing up internet exchange points all around the world."

"I know it sounds like a ludicrous thing to say, 1,000 SpaceXs, but if you said that about cloud, maybe it doesn't sound so ridiculous now."

@bridgitmendler w/ @itsmoislam

🇨🇳 #China Corporate Loan Rates Stay Below 3% for Liquidity - Financial News
- The rates underscore ample liquidity — and an accommodative monetary stance — to anchor financing costs and ensure credit supply across China’s economy, a Financial News report says.
- Corporate borrowing costs stayed at low levels in September, with the weighted average rate on new corporate loans slipping below 3% — about 20 bps lower than a year earlier: cites latest PBOC data.
- Decline in lending rates has outpaced policy-rate cuts since 2018, with corporate loan rates falling from roughly 5%-6% to around 3%.
- Efforts to disclose all borrowing-related fees are helping ensure lower rates translate into tangible funding-cost savings for businesses: cites unnamed industry sources.
